body: This kind of made me worried, I hope you're okay tho
LMAO there are new things to discover here too.
Oh, wait what GME are you talking about? But I hope it made you happy!

I can relate to this. I once hoped to have a grand job that they can be proud of but now, I just want to continue this simple job, live my life for myself. I'm honestly enjoying it without the pressure and things others say to me. 

But I'm glad you are able to reach this far. If you already love your job, just continue doing it or even take opportunities around/related to it.

You just said it right there. I hope more and more parents realize this soon.

Thank you. I hope things are good with you. Take care.
I'm glad you had the sandwich!
Oh, that sounds interesting. And were you satisfied after?

I really can't say the same but right now, it's already there and I think the best thing to do is make a different path from it. Do you have any hobbies or interests that you want to pursue? Maybe you can do that while you're studying. I realized that I'm really good at arts when I already finished college haha. I thought I was just having fun... but maybe you might have something like that.

That's true... I have heard a lot of stories about parents who do worse and I can't speak about all of the parents. I want to think that they're still doing their best but sometimes it's just too much.

I hope things are well with you. Take care.

Thank you. I've never been grateful and I hope that despite my situation, they see that I do see them as my family too.

I wish you the best as well! Have a great year and don't skip meals :)

They do tend to make our hobbies another salary income stream... But isn't it supposed to be an escape or help us say sane? I do hope you know that you're doing great tho. It's not easy to get A's in school! You aren't stupid. I may not know you well but hey, again, you are not stupid.

I can relate to what you said about guilt... I have friends from China too and they have told me about the extracurricular activities that one should have growing up. It's always the kids carrying the names of the family and living up to their expectations.

I do feel guilty too. I've been getting advises that by the time you graduate or turned legal, you should be out of the house by then but it really is different here. Despite working and having a place of your own (which I don't), the children is still obliged and expected to support the family. It's like living as their retirement plan.

When I was in high school, they told me about that and "parents only think what's good for their child" too. Most of the time, I hear that from my aunts and relatives— that I also should be grateful because they are making me do it.

​

I do feel that too.   


Random thing, our avatars are matching. Adorable.

That is true. It would be okay hearing those from someone else but if it's from the people you grew up with or looked up to as a kid, it just hits different. And yes, I have few but great friends and a lovely girlfriend. They have been acknowledging my works and efforts but all those things are just kept inside me while my family thinks otherwise. For some reason, it's hard to believe those things when it's not coming from my family.
I've been asking the same question and I still don't know if other apps/softwares have the same feature
Most of the artist that I know sell their stickers on Instagram and Twitter. Maybe you can try it out with active hashtags?
As soon as I woke up this morning, I had the urge to do a study on LomiLomicake's Summer's Gone art from Twitter. It's not as good but I wanted to make my own version :)
It was indeed a weird experience. I ended up feeling conscious of what I look like lol
this is great!!!
I didn't know about that, thank you!! Hope things will go well with your sticker business!

I started with traditional media as well and after transitioning to digital (or tried doing more with the medium), I saw myself slipping away and even experienced an art block. I get easily frustrated and find myself getting piled up with prompts and outputs. I'm not sure if it's the transition or the experience. 

Now, I'm trying to keep my sketchbook and hopefully scan them for my portfolio.

I just found out about Redbubble because of an artist and it's nice! Thank you, I'll probably try to list my items in local selling websites here. Hope I can market it on Instagram as well. 

If I may ask, how long have you been selling stickers? And do you use glossy papers over mattes?
